provenance: SEPARABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the accuracy on these rows should be read that way: single features reach one-vs-rest AUC 1.0000 for detector_blinding (sift_ratio, click_asymmetry), 0.9785 for intercept_resend (qber_mean) and 0.9703 for photon_number_splitting (multiphoton_rate), because the generator's _SIGNATURES table assigns each attack a distinctive value. This measures the simulator, not the world. SYNTHETIC QKD-attack telemetry generated by src/qsh/qml_ids/attacks.py. The eight classes are seven attack types plus normal traffic, a structure taken from Al-Kuwari et al. (arXiv:2509.14282); no number from that paper is reproduced here, and the 7 features and their values are this project's own. It is synthetic because no public real QKD-attack capture was found. Network-layer IDS corpora are a different problem: 5G-NIDD is CC BY 4.0 and trains this page's other model, UNSW-NB15 needs the authors' agreement, and the CIC's institute FAQ and its CICIDS2017 dataset page state conflicting terms. These synthetic rows are released under this repository's licence, Apache-2.0. This is the whole held-out quarter of the same seed-42 draw the published model was trained against, so the figure below is the model's own test metric rather than a resample of it.
split: the held-out quarter of the seed-42 stratified split, whole
modifications: Generated by this repository (qsh.qml_ids.attacks), not drawn from any published corpus: the held-out quarter of the seed-42 stratified split, all 600 rows, each value written as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same float32.

input.layout: samples[i] is one QKD session's features, in the order below

expected.note: Eight balanced classes, so the majority baseline is 1/8. The published comparison is macro F1, and that is what the in-run verification checks: aggregate accuracy is the metric that makes a broken detector look fine (Engelen et al., WTMC 2021), and it was what this sample published until Round 24i.

per_row.margin_is: the top output minus the runner-up, on the graph's own output
per_row.note: Each row's class by the page's rule and its margin to the decision boundary, from this file's samples, preprocessing and graph with onnxruntime; the page compares every row, and a different class within the tolerance of the boundary is a near tie, reported rather than failed.
